steps.body: Two angles sitting side by side, sharing a ray, **add together** to make one bigger angle. A 30° angle next to a 60° angle makes a combined angle of 30°+60°=**90°.** Angles combine exactly like any other measurement — just add.
Combine two neighboring angles into one larger turn.

widget.prompt: A 30° angle and a 45° angle sit side by side. Open the combined angle to their total.
widget.successFeedback: The combined angle is 75° because adjacent angle measures add: 30° + 45° = 75°.
widget.lowFeedback: The combined angle is wider. Add both measures.
widget.highFeedback: The angle is wider than the two pieces together.

predict.prompt: Two angles sit side by side sharing a ray. Do their measures ADD to make the combined angle?
predict.reveal: Angles glued along a shared ray pool their turns — the combined opening is the sum. Angle measure adds exactly the way lengths do.

explanationVariants: 70°+110°=180° — the two angles combine to a straight angle.
Adding the two measures gives the combined angle.

widget.prompt: A 70° angle sits next to a 110° angle. What is the combined angle?

commonErrors.feedback: 40 subtracts the angles. Adjacent angles ADD: 70+110=180.
That multiplies the two angles — combining side-by-side angles means adding: 70+110=180.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the two angle measures together.

steps.body: The combined angle can be **any size** — it doesn't have to land on a benchmark like 90° or 180°. A 25° angle next to a 35° angle simply makes 25°+35°=60°, nothing special required.

explanationVariants: 25°+35°=60° — a perfectly ordinary combined angle, no benchmark needed.
Adding still works the same way, benchmark or not.

widget.prompt: A 25° angle sits next to a 35° angle. What is the combined angle?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 subtracts the angles. Adjacent angles ADD: 25+35=60.
90 isn't the sum here — that would need different numbers. 25+35=60.

widget.prompt: Match each pair of adjacent angles to their combined total.

pairErrors.feedback: 90° belongs to the two pairs that make a right angle. 70°+110° combines to a straight angle: 180°.

widget.missFeedback: Add each pair of angle measures together.
widget.successFeedback: 45+45 and 40+50 both make 90°; 70+110 makes 180° — different pairs, different (or matching) totals.

explanationVariants: 20°+30°+40°=90° — three angles add together the same way two do.
Adding all three in a row gives the total combined angle.

widget.prompt: Three angles sit side by side, sharing rays: 20°, 30°, and 40°. What is their combined total?

commonErrors.feedback: 70 leaves out one of the three angles. Adding all three: 20+30+40=90.
That multiplies the angles together — but combining side-by-side angles always means adding: 20+30+40=90.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add all three angle measures together.

hints: Each panel of the fan is its own angle.
Add all three to find the fan's total opening.
explanationVariants: 35°+35°+40°=110° — the fan's three panels combine to its full opening angle.
Adding all three panel angles gives the total spread.

widget.prompt: A folding fan opens in 3 panels of 35°, 35°, and 40°. What is the fan's total opening angle?

commonErrors.feedback: 75 leaves out the third panel. Adding all three: 35+35+40=110.
5 subtracts instead of adding. The panels combine by addition: 35+35+40=110.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add all three panel angles together.

takeaways: Adjacent angles combine by adding their measures.
The combined angle can be any size — it doesn't need to land on a benchmark.
Three or more adjacent angles still just add, one after another.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Adjacent angles add together.** A 20° angle next to a 30° angle combines to 20°+30°=50°. No special benchmark required — just add the two measures.

explanationVariants: Adding the two angle measures gives the combined total.

widget.prompt: A 20° angle sits next to a 30° angle. What is the combined angle?

options.feedback: 10 subtracts instead of adding. Adjacent angles add: 20+30=50.
That multiplies the angles. Combining adjacent angles means adding: 20+30=50.
